chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan informed me, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ashyam, who said:
“Eating ushnaan melts away the body, rubbing oneself with pottery wears out the body, and using the siwak in the privy causes foul breath.”
Then he said, may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: whoever intends to urinate should seek out a place for it and avoid hard ground, for it causes it to splash back onto him. So this indicates that.

key_terms.السِّوَاكُ: the tooth-stick used for cleaning the teeth
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ الصُّلْبَةَ: hard ground that may cause urine to splash back
key_terms.الْأُشْنَانِ: a cleansing plant substance mentioned here as harmful to eat
key_terms.الْخَزَفِ: pottery or earthenware used here as something with which one rubs oneself
key_terms.الْخَلَاءِ: the privy or place of relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about etiquette and cleanliness when relieving oneself?
ai.summary: This hadith reports practical etiquettes related to bodily cleanliness and relieving oneself. It warns against certain harmful habits and indicates caution in choosing a suitable place for urination so that impurity does not return onto the body.
